relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a 9-year-old girl in whom NGS "revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20)".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no script transcribed tables (Table 1 is a single-patient lab table with timepoints as columns: 'On admission', 'On hospital day 2', 'After 9 months'; spans quote the row label through the 'On admission' cell). Rows: the index patient (label 'patient', rule 5; the text calls her 'the patient'/'our patient') and her father ('father of patient', rule 2), who is described as affected (recurrent fever and tonsillitis at preschool age) but was never tested, so he has no variant row. Mother and younger sister are mentioned only as refusing/not undergoing NGS, with no clinical description, so they get no rows. The other Korean HA20 patient (ref [8]) is mentioned only as a count ('only 2 patients, including our case') and gets no row. Ambiguities: the text says 'The c.547C>T variation of the proband was present in our patient' and the Fig. 1 legend says 'The c.547C>T mutation of the proband was detected in the patient'; it is unclear who 'the proband' is (possibly a previously reported proband, refs [4,6,7]); not interpreted. Fig. 1 legend spells the gene 'TNFIP3'; the text prints 'TNFAIP3'. The protein change is printed 'p.Arg183^*' in the text (Markdown superscript) and 'p.Arg183*' in the Fig. 1 legend. Zygosity and inheritance are not stated (parents refused testing). Age at diagnosis was recorded as the age at presentation ('A 9-year-old girl presented'), because the NGS diagnosis was made during the work-up of that presentation; the paper gives no separate age at diagnosis or at last evaluation (follow-up extends 9 months after colchicine). Country recorded from 'diagnosed with HA20 in Korea'; ancestry is not stated. Vital status 'alive' is inferred from 'Currently, we are considering treatments'. Anti-dsDNA IgG (22.6 and 12.8 IU/mL) and other numeric labs have no reference range or interpretation in the paper and were not recorded as features. Checklist: 'no uveitis' (narrow) left 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' as not reported; the father's 'no arthritis' and 'no recurrent diarrhea' left 'arthritis or arthralgia' and 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' as not reported. The patient's anal ulcer was counted as a gastrointestinal ulcer. PFAPA criteria ('absence of diarrhea, chest pain, skin rash, or arthritis') are diagnostic criteria, not patient findings, and were not used. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: tonsillectomy at 5 years of age (fever then recurred every 3 or 4 months); antipyretics; antibiotic treatment ineffective; colchicine, after which oral and genital ulcers disappeared at 9 months but fever continued to recur; immune suppressants (steroids, biologics) under consideration

antipyretics decreased body temperature but high fever occurred again during episode
Antibiotic treatment was ineffective.
Colchicine was started, and 9 months after treatment, oral and genital ulcers disappeared. However, the fever continued to recur every 3 or 4 months.
Currently, we are considering treatments with immune suppressants such as steroids and biologics.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic testing: NGS for genes related to periodic fever and autoinflammatory syndromes revealed a nonsense mutation in TNFAIP3; initially suspected (misdiagnosed) as Kikuchi disease with PFAPA syndrome
span: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) for genes related to periodic fever and autoinflammatory syndromes was conducted to identify a possible genetic disorder.
It revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20) (Fig. 1).
Initially, we suspected Kikuchi disease with periodic fever, aphthous stomatitis, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis (PFAPA) syndrome
